A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the lepton number violation is not a good signature for the majority of neutrino mass models, except for the inverse seesaw model, and the neutrinoless double beta decay is the most powerful probe for the majority of models.

we have performed a comprehensive survey of the effective field theory (EFT) operators that are consistent with the minimal Standard Model (SM) particle content and gauge group and which generate neutrino masses via radiative corrections.

we have calculated the characteristic cutoff energy scale associated with each of 129 lepton-number violating effective operators, of mass dimension 5-11, consistent with the standard model gauge and particle content, and we have used these cutoffs to calculate the observable manifestations of these lepton-number violating effects in neutrinoless double beta decay, rare meson, gauge boson, and lepton decays, and at hadron and lepton colliders.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the current and future data from a variety of experimental probes will be able to provide a wealth of information regarding the underlying model of neutrino masses, and in particular the nature of the lepton number violating processes which generate the neutrino mass matrix.
the LHC and ILC will be very powerful tools for probing lepton number violation, and in particular, will be able to probe a number of operators that are not accessible to current experiments.
lepton number violation can be probed in many ways.
